ownership_and_exit_count_assumption.generic_disjoint_payment_limit: N distinct payers and N distinct recipients can require separate sender-change exits as well as recipient exits, potentially2N exits. Different owners' claims cannot be merged by collecting their private witnesses. Those additional exits are not priced by the N-exit table.
ownership_and_exit_count_assumption.no_manufactured_demand_or_denominator: A synthetic payment cycle is not evidence of real demand or new useful principal. Do not manufacture a ring, omit sender-change exits, count retained principal/refunds as new payments, or enlarge the frozen useful-net denominator to claim a fee pass.
ownership_and_exit_count_assumption.reference_pattern: The observed N2 cross-payment pattern has each actor own both an incoming recipient claim and that same actor's own change. Each original backup therefore consumes two real claims in one private exit. The N-exit counterfactual assumes that same ownership/claim pattern, not generic N disjoint payers and recipients.

unperformed_or_unpriced_costs_and_limits: Only N2 is implemented and genuinely proved. The selected guest, record codec and native W currently require exactly two children; N8/N16 are not accepted by that profile.

A larger count changes guest image and native program constants/body shape. New source/design selection, exact public transcript checks, real quote and genuine proof/native validation would be required. No such work ran for this addendum.

The table holds W bytes, framing, B1600, child record width and private exit shapes fixed. Future byte overhead, script-unit requirements, capacity/NF/history behavior or storage mass can change costs; storage is explicitly assumed not dominant.

B1500 continuing/terminal reference costs are actual N2 owner measurements, not universal larger-batch exit quotes. B1600 reference adds the source-derived budget delta of10000mass/1000000sompi; no newB1600 proof is claimed.

The N-exit reference pattern requires the explicit same-owner incoming+change ownership assumption above. Generic disjoint payers/recipients may need2N exits; that case is not priced and no witness gathering or sender-change exit discount is assumed.

The N-minus1 continuing plus one terminal pattern is a counterfactual average, not a promised payout schedule or fee allocation. All modeled aggregate amounts are integer sompi; percentage strings are display-only.

Funding/entry fees remain unknown; operator charges, data availability, hardware/proving expense, latency, contention, inclusion/currentness, storage under changed amounts and independent distribution/retention are not priced. No full-lifecycle2percent pass follows.
Private unilateral low-demand behavior is not improved by assuming a larger batch. No REVEAL substitution or privacy/accepted-chain/mainnet/security claim follows.
